nodes.description: EIF2AK2 encodes the double-stranded-RNA-activated protein kinase PKR, an eIF2-alpha kinase of the integrated stress response. Dystonia-associated missense variants lie in functional domains of PKR and produce abnormally prolonged, enhanced activation of the kinase rather than loss of activity.

nodes.description: Onset or stepwise worsening of dystonia has been reported after febrile or viral illness, and also after surgery or general anesthesia. Viral double-stranded RNA is the physiological activator of PKR, which makes infection a plausible trigger for further stress-response activation, but this has not been tested in patients or models. The exposure binding covers the viral component only; the surgery and anesthesia reports are recorded here in prose.

nodes.description: Patient-derived fibroblasts carrying EIF2AK2 dystonia variants show abnormally enhanced and prolonged PKR-mediated phosphorylation of eIF2-alpha (Ser51) and sustained activation of the integrated stress response. A dysregulated eIF2-alpha pathway is a convergence point shared with other monogenic dystonias (DYT-PRKRA, DYT-TOR1A, DYT-THAP1). The only cell-level measurement is in patient skin fibroblasts; activation in neurons or the basal ganglia, and any effect on translation, have not been measured.
